claim: Chromosome segregation requires assembly of the mitotic spindle, a dynamic microtubule-based force-generating machine.
source: Chromosome segregation is a mechanical process that requires assembly of the mitotic spindle – a dynamic microtubule-based force-generating machine.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a fundamental description of the process.

claim: Connections to the mitotic spindle are mediated by sister kinetochore pairs that form dynamic end-on attachments to microtubules emanating from opposite spindle poles.
source: Connections to this spindle are mediated by sister kinetochore pairs, that form dynamic end-on attachments to microtubules emanating from opposite spindle poles.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract describing the mechanism of spindle-kinetochore connection.

claim: Bi-orientation generates forces that have been reported to stretch the kinetochore itself.
source: This bi-orientation generates forces that have been reported to stretch the kinetochore itself, which has been suggested to stabilise attachment and silence the spindle checkpoint.
evidence: This claim references prior reports in the literature about kinetochore stretching.

claim: Kinetochore stretching has been suggested to stabilise attachment and silence the spindle checkpoint.
source: This bi-orientation generates forces that have been reported to stretch the kinetochore itself, which has been suggested to stabilise attachment and silence the spindle checkpoint.
evidence: This claim references prior suggestions in the literature about the functional role of kinetochore stretching.

claim: The outer kinetochore domain can swivel around the inner kinetochore/centromere.
source: We reveal using three dimensional tracking that the outer kinetochore domain can swivel around the inner kinetochore/centromere, which results in large reductions in intra-kinetochore distance (delta) when viewed in lower dimensions.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on 3D tracking experiments.

claim: Swiveling of the outer kinetochore domain results in large reductions in intra-kinetochore distance (delta) when viewed in lower dimensions.
source: We reveal using three dimensional tracking that the outer kinetochore domain can swivel around the inner kinetochore/centromere, which results in large reductions in intra-kinetochore distance (delta) when viewed in lower dimensions.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study demonstrating the effect of projection on delta measurements.

claim: Swivel provides a mechanical flexibility that enables kinetochores at the periphery of the spindle to engage microtubules.
source: We show that swivel provides a mechanical flexibility that enables kinetochores at the periphery of the spindle to engage microtubules.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on analysis of swivel at different spindle positions.

claim: Swivel reduces as cells approach anaphase.
source: Swivel reduces as cells approach anaphase, suggesting an organisational change linked to checkpoint satisfaction and/or obligatory changes in kinetochore mechanochemistry may occur before dissolution of sister chromatid cohesion.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on analysis of swivel during metaphase progression.

claim: The reduction in swivel as cells approach anaphase suggests an organisational change linked to checkpoint satisfaction and/or obligatory changes in kinetochore mechanochemistry may occur before dissolution of sister chromatid cohesion.
source: Swivel reduces as cells approach anaphase, suggesting an organisational change linked to checkpoint satisfaction and/or obligatory changes in kinetochore mechanochemistry may occur before dissolution of sister chromatid cohesion.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the swivel reduction data, presented as a speculation about its biological significance.

claim: The core kinetochore structure assembles in a hierarchical fashion with the CCAN physically bridging CENP-A containing chromatin and the microtubule-binding KMN network.
source: Extensive biochemical work has assembled a detailed parts list for the kinetochore and we now understand that the core structure assembles in a hierarchical fashion with the CCAN (constitutive centromere associated network) physically bridging CENP-A containing chromatin and the microtubule-binding KMN network (KNL1, MIS12 and NDC80 complexes) (Pesenti et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pesenti et al., 2016.

claim: Multiple copies of each kinetochore component produce a supramolecular disk-shaped assembly with a metaphase diameter of ~200 nm and a depth of ~100 nm.
source: Multiple copies of each component (Suzuki et al., 2015) produce a supramolecular disk-shaped assembly with a (metaphase) diameter of ~200 nm and a depth of ~100 nm (Rieder and Salmon, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Suzuki et al., 2015 and Rieder and Salmon, 1998.

claim: Removing microtubule-pulling forces in both human and Drosophila cells has been shown to reduce the distance between centromeric chromatin and the microtubule-binding outer layer of the kinetochore by ~30 nm.
source: Removing microtubule-pulling forces in both human and Drosophila cells has been shown to reduce the distance between centromeric chromatin and the microtubule-binding outer layer of the kinetochore by ~30 nm (Wan et al., 2009; Maresca and Salmon, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wan et al., 2009 and Maresca and Salmon, 2009.

claim: The reduction in intra-kinetochore distance upon removing microtubule-pulling forces is interpreted as evidence of tension within the kinetochore generated by microtubule pulling.
source: This is interpreted as evidence of tension within the kinetochore generated by microtubule pulling, an event that has been linked to how kinetochores stabilise correct microtubule attachments and silence the spindle assembly checkpoint (Joglekar et al., 2009; Maresca and Salmon, 2009; Uchida et al., 2009; Drpic et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim references prior interpretations in the literature supported by multiple citations.

claim: The requirement for intra-kinetochore tension in the checkpoint silencing mechanism has recently been challenged.
source: However, the requirement for this intra-kinetochore tension in the checkpoint silencing mechanism has recently been challenged (Etemad et al., 2015; Tauchman et al., 2015; Magidson et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Etemad et al., 2015, Tauchman et al., 2015, and Magidson et al., 2016.

claim: Live cell imaging of proteins in the inner and outer domains of the kinetochore in PtK2 cells revealed that the kinetochore is compressed (rather than stretched) when under pulling force.
source: Counter intuitively, live cell imaging of proteins in the inner and outer domains of the kinetochore in PtK2 cells revealed that the kinetochore is compressed (rather than stretched) when under pulling force (Dumont et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dumont et al., 2012.

claim: Following bi-orientation, delta does not increase or decrease as the inter-sister distance increases, suggesting that the kinetochore is non-compliant.
source: Moreover, following bi-orientation Δ does not increase or decrease as the inter-sister distance increases (the latter is known to vary under the forces acting on kinetochores during metaphase oscillations) suggesting that the kinetochore is now non-compliant (Suzuki et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Suzuki et al., 2014.

claim: The 3D Euclidean distance between eGFP-CENP-A and Ndc80-tagRFP spot centres (Δ3D) for sister kinetochore pairs in live cells was estimated to be 98.0 (± 0.9) nm.
source: The 3D Euclidean distance Δ between eGFP and tagRFP spot centres (Δ3D) for sister kinetochore pairs in live cells was estimated to be 98.0 (± 0.9) nm (n = 4291; Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary measurement from the study's 3D tracking experiments, shown in Figure 1D.

claim: No difference was detected between away-from-the-pole (AP) and poleward (P) moving kinetochores in 3D measurements of delta in human cells.
source: Unlike in PtK2 cells (Dumont et al., 2012) we did not detect a difference between away-from-the-pole (AP) and poleward (P) moving kinetochores in either 3D (Figure 1E) or 2D measurements (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's analysis, shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The 3D measurement of CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) distance is somewhat larger than the ~60 nm predicted from previous measurements of CENP-A-to-Spc24 distance.
source: Our 3D measurement is somewhat larger than the ~60 nm predicted from previous measurements of CENP-A-to-Spc24 distance (Suzuki et al., 2014) and the position of the Ndc80 C-terminus based on electron microscopy of the purified complex (Wei et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim compares the study's measurement to prior measurements cited from Suzuki et al., 2014 and Wei et al., 2005.

claim: Applying the same 1D method to the 3D data gives a distance of 57.9 (± 1.1) nm, indicating that projection effects (3D to 1D) may be giving a misleading picture of kinetochore structure/architecture.
source: However, the CENP-A-to-Spc24 measurement in Suzuki et al. was effectively one-dimensional (Δ1D, see supplemental discussion); applying the same 1D method to our data gives a distance of 57.9 (± 1.1) nm (n = 1002; Figure 1D) indicating that projection effects (3D to 1D) may be giving a misleading picture of kinetochore structure/architecture.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study comparing 3D and 1D measurements, shown in Figure 1D.

claim: No correlation was found between Δ3D and changes in inter-kinetochore distance during kinetochore oscillations in metaphase, indicating that the CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) connection is non-compliant (stiff).
source: To examine compliance under tension we analysed the correlation of Δ3D with the changes in inter-kinetochore distance that take place during kinetochore oscillations in metaphase. We found no correlation (Figure 1F) indicating that the CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) connection is indeed non-compliant (stiff).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's analysis, shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Treatment with 3 µM nocodazole for 2 hr resulted in a 30% decrease (283 nm) in inter-kinetochore distance.
source: We found that despite a 30% decrease (283 nm) in inter-kinetochore distance, d (Figure 2B), Δ3D was only marginally reduced by 5% (5 nm, significant at p = 0.012, n ≥ 649 for each condition).
evidence: This is a primary measurement from the study's nocodazole treatment experiments, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Treatment with 3 µM nocodazole for 2 hr resulted in Δ3D being only marginally reduced by 5% (5 nm) for the CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) linkage.
source: We found that despite a 30% decrease (283 nm) in inter-kinetochore distance, d (Figure 2B), Δ3D was only marginally reduced by 5% (5 nm, significant at p = 0.012, n ≥ 649 for each condition).
evidence: This is a primary measurement from the study's nocodazole treatment experiments, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The small change in Δ3D for the CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) linkage under nocodazole is consistent with the only other live measurement of Δ in human cells (between CENP-A and mCherry-Mis12) where Δ2D decreased marginally under nocodazole.
source: This small change in Δ3D for the CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) linkage is consistent with the only other live measurement of Δ in human cells (between CENP-A and mCherry-Mis12) where Δ2D decreased marginally under nocodazole (Uchida et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim compares the study's finding to a prior measurement cited from Uchida et al., 2009.

claim: 3D measurement between eGFP-CENP-A and mCherry-Mis12, and between GFP-CENP-C and Ndc80(C), produced 5–7 nm reductions in Δ3D under nocodazole treatment.
source: Our own 3D measurement between these same markers, and also between GFP-CENP-C and Ndc80(C), produced the same marginal 5–7 nm reductions in Δ3D (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary measurement from the study's experiments with different markers, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: In paraformaldehyde fixed cells, the distance between CENP-A and the position of the MIS12 complex (using anti-Nnf1 antibodies) was reduced by 5 nm under nocodazole treatment.
source: In paraformaldehyde fixed cells the distance between CENP-A and the position of the MIS12 complex (using anti-Nnf1 antibodies) was also reduced by 5 nm, while both eGFP-CENP-A and endogenous CENP-A (using anti-CENP-A antibodies) to Ndc80(C) give marginal changes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary measurement from the study's immunofluorescence experiments, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Microtubule-pulling forces do not dramatically stretch the kinetochore and the intra-kinetochore linkages are relatively stiff.
source: We conclude that microtubule-pulling forces do not dramatically stretch the kinetochore and that the intra-kinetochore linkages are relatively stiff.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's measurements of delta under various conditions.

claim: The outer domain of the kinetochore is non-compliant.
source: This is consistent with previous work showing that the outer domain is non-compliant (Suzuki et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Suzuki et al., 2014.

claim: The distance from eGFP-CENP-A and GFP-CENP-C to the amino (N)-terminal end of Ndc80 in live cells showed a ~15 nm reduction in Δ3D following nocodazole treatment.
source: We next tested whether there are changes in the outer domain of the kinetochore by determining the distance from eGFP-CENP-A and GFP-CENP-C to the amino (N)-terminal end of Ndc80 in live cells. We detected a ~15 nm reduction in Δ3D following nocodazole treatment, with up to half of this contributed from the change in the inner domain discussed above (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary measurement from the study's experiments with N-terminal Ndc80 markers, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) measurement for Δ1D decreased by 70% from 57.9 (± 1.1) nm in untreated cells to 17.8 (± 4.4) nm in nocodazole treated cells.
source: For example, the CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) measurement for Δ1D decreased by 70% from 57.9 (± 1.1) nm in untreated cells to 17.8 (± 4.4) nm in nocodazole treated cells.
evidence: This is a primary measurement from the study comparing 1D measurements under different conditions.

claim: The 40 nm change observed in 1D is considerably more than the 5 nm (5%) changes in Δ3D.
source: This 40 nm change observed in 1D is considerably more than the 5 nm (5%) changes in Δ3D.
evidence: This is a comparison of measurements from the study highlighting the discrepancy between 1D and 3D measurements.

claim: The discrepancy between Δ1D and Δ3D suggests that a rotation is present and that this is the major degree of freedom upon microtubule attachment (rather than the stretching of the kinetochore).
source: The observed discrepancy between Δ1D and Δ3D suggests that a rotation is present and that this is the major degree of freedom upon microtubule attachment (rather than the stretching of the kinetochore).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the measurement discrepancy, inferring the presence of rotation.

claim: Calculation of swivel across all untreated kinetochores yielded a median of 51.6° as compared to 73.8° in 3 µM nocodazole.
source: Calculation of swivel across all untreated kinetochores yielded a median of 51.6° as compared to 73.8° in 3 µM nocodazole (Figure 3B) – this difference is significant (p < 10–4) and explains the decrease in the 1D measurement of Δ in nocodazole-treated cells.
evidence: This is a primary measurement from the study's swivel analysis, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The difference in swivel between untreated and nocodazole-treated cells is significant (p < 10–4) and explains the decrease in the 1D measurement of Δ in nocodazole-treated cells.
source: Calculation of swivel across all untreated kinetochores yielded a median of 51.6° as compared to 73.8° in 3 µM nocodazole (Figure 3B) – this difference is significant (p < 10–4) and explains the decrease in the 1D measurement of Δ in nocodazole-treated cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's statistical analysis of swivel measurements, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: 3 µM nocodazole treatment results in a larger range of y-directional swivel (population standard deviation = 56.4° in untreated vs. 89.5° in 3 µM nocodazole).
source: This measurement showed that 3 µM nocodazole treatment results in a larger range of y-directional swivel (population standard deviation = 56.4° in untreated vs. 89.5° in 3 µM nocodazole), with some outer kinetochores capable of rotating inside the eGFP signal (i.e. y-swivel > 90°; Figure 3C), which explains the presence of negative measurements for Δ1D.
evidence: This is a primary measurement from the study's y-directional swivel analysis, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Some outer kinetochores are capable of rotating inside the eGFP signal (i.e. y-swivel > 90°) under nocodazole treatment, which explains the presence of negative measurements for Δ1D.
source: This measurement showed that 3 µM nocodazole treatment results in a larger range of y-directional swivel (population standard deviation = 56.4° in untreated vs. 89.5° in 3 µM nocodazole), with some outer kinetochores capable of rotating inside the eGFP signal (i.e. y-swivel > 90°; Figure 3C), which explains the presence of negative measurements for Δ1D.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's swivel analysis explaining negative delta measurements, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The increase in 3D swivel and broadening of y-directional swivel using CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) were also seen in 10 µM taxol-treated cells, albeit to a lesser extent.
source: This increase in 3D swivel and broadening of y-directional swivel using CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) were also seen in 10 µM taxol-treated cells, albeit to a lesser extent (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's taxol treatment experiments, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Loss of microtubule pulling force is sufficient to increase swivel, although loss of microtubule-kinetochore attachment increases swivel still further.
source: This condition leaves the spindle intact and suggests that loss of microtubule pulling force is sufficient to increase swivel, although loss of microtubule-kinetochore attachment increases swivel still further.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the taxol and nocodazole treatment data comparing their effects on swivel.

claim: Y-swivel changes over time demonstrating that kinetochores do not have a fixed swivel.
source: Furthermore, y-swivel changes over time demonstrating that kinetochores do not have a fixed swivel, swivel potentially adapting to changes in microtubule attachment, microtubule forces and sister kinetochore dynamics (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's time-lapse analysis, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Swivel potentially adapts to changes in microtubule attachment, microtubule forces and sister kinetochore dynamics.
source: Furthermore, y-swivel changes over time demonstrating that kinetochores do not have a fixed swivel, swivel potentially adapting to changes in microtubule attachment, microtubule forces and sister kinetochore dynamics (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of dynamic swivel based on the time-lapse data.

claim: Kinetochore pairs at the centre of the metaphase plate exhibited a smaller degree of swivel compared to those at the periphery.
source: We found that kinetochore pairs at the centre of the metaphase plate exhibited a smaller degree of swivel compared to those at the periphery (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's spatial analysis of swivel, shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Plotting y-directional swivel against the position along the metaphase plate in the y-axis demonstrated that kinetochores begin to exhibit swivel towards their attached spindle pole.
source: Plotting y-directional swivel against the position along the metaphase plate in the y-axis demonstrated that kinetochores begin to exhibit swivel towards their attached spindle pole (Figure 4B), a phenomenon that is more evident once kinetochore pairs are beyond 4 µm from the centre of the metaphase plate.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's spatial analysis of swivel, shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The eGFP, tagRFP and k-fibre signals were approximately co-linear, with the angles tended on the inter-sister axis by the k-fibre (ϑkMT) and intra-kinetochore axes (ϑy-swivel) being significantly correlated (r = 0.371, p < 10–4).
source: The eGFP, tagRFP and k-fibre signals were approximately co-linear, with the angles tended on the inter-sister axis by the k-fibre (ϑkMT) and intra-kinetochore axes (ϑy-swivel) being significantly correlated (r = 0.371, p < 10–4; Figure 4C, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's immunofluorescence analysis correlating swivel with k-fiber direction, shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Outer kinetochore swivel can be used as a proxy for the direction in which the k-fibres are bound by the kinetochore.
source: This shows that outer kinetochore swivel can be used as a proxy for the direction in which the k-fibres are bound by the kinetochore – this is not surprising as Ndc80 binds microtubules directly.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the correlation between swivel and k-fiber direction, with reasoning based on known Ndc80 function.

claim: The thickness of the metaphase plate reduces as a cell transits metaphase and approaches anaphase onset.
source: To do this we took advantage of the observation that the thickness of the metaphase plate reduces as a cell transits metaphase and approaches anaphase onset (Jaqaman et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Jaqaman et al., 2010.

claim: Swivel clearly decreases as a cell moves through metaphase.
source: Fitting a sheet to this data reveals how swivel clearly decreases as a cell moves through metaphase (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's analysis of swivel during metaphase progression, shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Peripheral kinetochores decreased absolute y-swivel from 45.7 (± 1.9) ° (n = 455) in early metaphase to 33.6 (± 1.4) ° (n = 460) in late metaphase (p < 10–4).
source: Binning the plate thicknesses allowed a statistical comparison that peripheral kinetochores decreased absolute y-swivel from 45.7 (± 1.9) ° (n = 455) in early metaphase to 33.6 (± 1.4) ° (n = 460) in late metaphase (p < 10–4; Figure 4E and F, and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary measurement from the study's analysis of swivel during metaphase progression, shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: Δ1D increases from early to late metaphase, suggesting that swivel can explain changes in intra-kinetochore stretch (1D) that have been linked to SAC silencing.
source: We can also confirm that Δ1D increases from early to late metaphase (Figure 4E, and Figure 4—source data 1), again suggesting that swivel can explain changes in intra-kinetochore stretch (1D) that have been linked to SAC silencing.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's analysis of delta during metaphase progression, shown in Figure 4E, with interpretation linking it to swivel.

claim: Δ3D (CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C)) does not increase as metaphase progresses.
source: On the other hand, Δ3D (CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C)) does not increase as metaphase progresses (Figure 4E), further highlighting how swivel is the distinctive mechanical change in kinetochore structure that correlates with time of anaphase onset.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's analysis of delta during metaphase progression, shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Swivel is the distinctive mechanical change in kinetochore structure that correlates with time of anaphase onset.
source: On the other hand, Δ3D (CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C)) does not increase as metaphase progresses (Figure 4E), further highlighting how swivel is the distinctive mechanical change in kinetochore structure that correlates with time of anaphase onset.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's findings comparing swivel and delta changes during metaphase progression.

claim: It is unknown whether the swivel of the outer kinetochore has any direct role in the SAC silencing mechanism or whether it is a downstream event associated with the falling Cdk1-CyclinB activity that follows SAC satisfaction.
source: At this stage it is unknown whether the swivel of the outer kinetochore has any direct role in the SAC silencing mechanism or whether it is a downstream event associated with the falling Cdk1-CyclinB activity that follows SAC satisfaction (Clute and Pines, 1999).
evidence: This is an explicit statement of uncertainty about the causal relationship between swivel and SAC silencing, with citation to Clute and Pines, 1999.

claim: Changes in swivel, being substantially greater than 3D distance changes, provide a proximity change between Aurora B and its substrates.
source: What our data does suggest is that changes in swivel, being substantially greater than 3D distance changes, provide a proximity change between Aurora B and its substrates.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's findings suggesting a potential mechanism involving Aurora B.

claim: Kinetochores are undergoing a shift in their mechanochemical status in readiness for the imminent onset of anaphase.
source: It is also tempting to speculate that kinetochores are undergoing a shift in their mechanochemical status in readiness for the imminent onset of anaphase.
evidence: This is an explicit speculation about the functional significance of the observed changes.

claim: Kinetochore speeds decrease as anaphase approaches.
source: As well as the swivel changes reported here, this may also directly relate to the observation that kinetochore speeds decrease as anaphase approaches (Jaqaman et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Jaqaman et al., 2010.

claim: The swivelling of the outer kinetochore requires a flexible structure that at the same time is non-compliant under varying load.
source: From a mechanical perspective, the swivelling of the outer kinetochore requires a flexible structure, that at the same time is non-compliant under varying load.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanical properties required to explain the observed swivel behavior.

claim: One possibility is that the outer kinetochore can move and remodel relative to the fixed surface of the inner kinetochore.
source: One possibility is that the outer kinetochore can move and remodel relative to the fixed surface of the inner kinetochore (Figure 4G(ii)) as recently shown (Wynne and Funabiki, 2015; Magidson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of swivel, supported by citations to Wynne and Funabiki, 2015 and Magidson et al., 2016.

claim: We cannot rule out that we are observing a complete rotation of the whole kinetochore structure within the chromosome.
source: We cannot rule out that we are observing a complete rotation of the whole kinetochore structure within the chromosome (Figure 4G(ii)).
evidence: This is an explicit statement of an alternative explanation that cannot be ruled out.

claim: The positive correlation in the tilt of elliptical CENP-A and Ndc80 fluorescence signals in fixed cell imaging supports the idea of complete rotation of the whole kinetochore structure within the chromosome.
source: This idea is supported by the positive correlation in the tilt of elliptical CENP-A and Ndc80 fluorescence signals in fixed cell imaging (Wan et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wan et al., 2009.

claim: The fact that swivelling is most extreme on unattached kinetochores suggests that it may optimise the microtubule search-and-capture process.
source: The fact that swivelling is most extreme on unattached kinetochores suggests that it may optimise the microtubule search-and-capture process (Figure 4G(i)) – this would have a similar effect to broadening of the microtubule-binding region of the kinetochore, as has been implicated in the timing and accuracy of search-and-capture (Zaytsev et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional role of swivel in microtubule capture, with citation to Zaytsev et al., 2015.

claim: Kinetochore dynamics were normal following exogenous expression of Ndc80-tagRFP.
source: We confirmed that kinetochore dynamics were normal following exogenous expression of Ndc80-tagRFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a control experiment confirming that the fluorescent tagging did not perturb kinetochore function, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) linkage was not affected following treatment with 10 µM taxol (p = 0.302).
source: Interestingly, the CENP-A-to-Ndc80(C) linkage was not affected following treatment with 10 µM taxol (p = 0.302; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's taxol treatment experiments, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Exerting pulling force on the kinetochore is not sufficient to change Δ3D.
source: This demonstrates that exerting pulling force on the kinetochore is not sufficient to change Δ3D and suggests that it is the presence of microtubules that induces a conformational change in the kinetochore.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the taxol treatment data.

claim: It is the presence of microtubules that induces a conformational change in the kinetochore.
source: This demonstrates that exerting pulling force on the kinetochore is not sufficient to change Δ3D and suggests that it is the presence of microtubules that induces a conformational change in the kinetochore.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the taxol treatment data suggesting a mechanism.

claim: The additional movement of the Ndc80 N-terminus may relate to the conformational change in the NDC80 complex that has been reported in budding yeast.
source: The additional movement of the Ndc80 N-terminus may relate to the conformational change in the NDC80 complex that has been reported in budding yeast (Aravamudhan et al., 2015) although further experiments will be needed to confirm this.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of the observed N-terminal movement, with citation to Aravamudhan et al., 2015.

claim: The delta change for CENP-A/CENP-C to Ndc80 N-terminus is smaller than that seen in fixed cells.
source: This delta change is smaller than that seen in fixed cells (see Etemad et al., 2015, and Figure 1—source data 1) a difference that may reflect the reported effects of fixation on kinetochore integrity/epitope accessibility (Magidson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a comparison between live and fixed cell measurements, with citations to Etemad et al., 2015 and Magidson et al., 2016.

claim: The difference between live and fixed cell delta measurements may reflect the reported effects of fixation on kinetochore integrity/epitope accessibility.
source: This delta change is smaller than that seen in fixed cells (see Etemad et al., 2015, and Figure 1—source data 1) a difference that may reflect the reported effects of fixation on kinetochore integrity/epitope accessibility (Magidson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculation about the cause of the difference, with citation to Magidson et al., 2016.

claim: Attaching fluorescent markers to Ndc80's N-terminus causes perturbed force generation in live cells.
source: This contrasts to previous work showing that attaching fluorescent markers to Ndc80's N-terminus causes perturbed force generation in live cells (Mattiuzzo et al., 2011); we only use the mCherry-Ndc80 construct here for completeness.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mattiuzzo et al., 2011.

claim: Changes in delta under different physiological conditions need to be interpreted with caution as the shape and size of kinetochore domains are subject to change.
source: However, changes in delta under different physiological conditions need to be interpreted with caution as the shape and size of kinetochore domains are subject to change (see Magidson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a cautionary statement about interpretation, with citation to Magidson et al., 2016.
